I am weighing whether to trade my GOOJF card for $50 cash to survive these low-rent squares without selling houses.

No opponent seems likely to buy the GOOJF card for cash. Player 2 already rejected a $50 offer, and player 4 probably values the card little since jail is already a safe haven. Player 3 has no cash to spend. Proposing a trade wastes one action but not the game turn, and opponents already know I have only $23. I do not need more properties, so pairing the card with another asset would not help.

Player 2 is the main threat. Their red properties charge $700–$1100 in rent, and landing there would be fatal unless I sell many houses. From Vermont Avenue, I do not roll onto any red squares this turn.

I will end my turn now to preserve the housing lock. I do not need to sell any houses unless debt forces it next turn.

If I must sell a house next turn, I will prefer Tennessee Avenue over New York Avenue. Dropping Tennessee from four houses to three lowers rent from $750 to $550, while dropping New York from four to three lowers it from $800 to $600.
